prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures the continuous ground plane receding across an indoor sports hall, showing the camera wearer approaching a badminton net from about 3–4 m away in frame 1 to roughly 2 m in frame 2, looking straight down at their own shoes, a racket tip, and a shuttlecock within 1–1.5 m in frame 3, and then turning right in frames 4–5 toward a teammate on their side of the court. In frames 1–2, a basketball hoop stand sits 5–6 m away on the far left and two opponents stand behind the net at roughly 6–8 m on the left and 5–7 m on the right (about 4–5 m apart from each other), whereas in frames 4–5 a teammate holding a racket within her arm's reach approaches on the right from roughly 3.5 m to 2 m while facing and looking toward the camera wearer. In frame 3, the camera wearer's own racket at the bottom right is within arm's reach and mostly out of view, while an opponent's legs are cropped at the top left about 2.5–3 m away behind the net. Compared to RGB, the depth map clearly separates the foreground net post, top tape, and nearby teammate's silhouette—including her thin racket shaft in frames 4–5—from the distant background wall over 10–15 m away. However, the depth map is unreliable on the painted floor lines in frame 3, which it falsely renders as raised bright ridges, and on the see-through badminton net mesh, which disappears into the floor depth.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete people across the court: two opponents behind the net in frames 1–2 (one on the left at 6–8 m and one on the right at 5–7 m, standing 4–5 m apart and facing toward the camera wearer), and a nearby teammate in front on the right in frames 4–5 who steps closer from about 3.5 m to 2 m while facing the camera wearer. The segmentation masks in frames 1–2 show the right-hand opponent partially occluded by the top tape of the badminton net, and in frame 5 the map detects tiny distant figures in the far background on the left (15–20 m away) that are hard to notice at a glance in the RGB strip. However, the map completely misses all sports equipment—including the basketball stand, the badminton net and posts, the shuttlecock on the floor in frames 3 and 5, and the rackets held within arm's reach of the players and the camera wearer. It also fails to segment the partially visible opponent's legs at the top left and the camera wearer's feet at the bottom of frame 3. Furthermore, it is unreliable on the gymnasium floor in frame 5, where it hallucinates a painted court circle at roughly 10–12 m as a 'sink'.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map tracks the 2D joint configuration of only the nearby teammate on the right side of the court in frames 4 and 5, as she approaches from roughly 3.5 m to 2 m in front of the camera wearer. The yellow body keypoints show her upright posture, torso, and head oriented toward the camera wearer, with her right arm extended downward holding a racket within her arm's reach and her left arm bent near her waist as her legs step forward across the floor. This skeletal wireframe makes her exact limb articulation, shoulder orientation, and weight shift between frames 4 and 5 easier to read than against her dark clothing in the RGB image. However, the pose map is completely blank in frames 1–3, failing to detect the two opponents 5–8 m away across the net in frames 1–2, the partially visible person at the top left of frame 3, the camera wearer's own feet at the bottom of frame 3, or the distant background people 15–20 m away in frames 4–5. It also fails to render any magenta hand skeletons on the nearby teammate in frames 4–5 and provides no spatial information about the court boundaries, net, basketball hoop, or rackets.
